subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What guarantee should OpenClaw advertise and enforce for private sessions: transcript-only non-persistence, or a comprehensive no-private-workspace-read and no-durable-content-write boundary across core and plugins?
rationale: Source inspection proves the capability is missing, but only maintainers can define the threat model, allowed operational metadata, provider/network behavior, channel activation policy, and whether plugins must fail closed when they cannot honor the mode.

options.title: Comprehensive private session
options.body: Create a per-session contract that blocks private workspace and memory reads plus durable content writes, allowing only narrowly documented operational metadata.

options.title: Transcript-only ephemeral session
options.body: Keep transcripts in memory but explicitly exclude workspace access, tools, plugins, logs, media, and provider traffic from the guarantee.

options.title: Decline an incognito guarantee
options.body: Retain context-injection, retention, and deletion controls and document that OpenClaw does not provide an enforceable private-session boundary.

recommendation.title: Comprehensive private session
recommendation.body: Create a per-session contract that blocks private workspace and memory reads plus durable content writes, allowing only narrowly documented operational metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior canonical review and recent session/memory lifecycle work make this the strongest available owner for the cross-cutting product and security decision.
